title: Quarterly stability forum and pilot risk inventory
summary: Quarterly check-in focused on stability signals, a catalog of pilot risks for the upcoming model transition, and a prioritized set of mitigation actions. Discussed recent usage spike, unexpected cost delta in embeddings, a P1 latency regression on dedicated pool, and next steps for a staged pilot with stress tests and finance alignment.
topics: Embedding cost variance and billing reconciliation
P1 latency regression on dedicated pool
Pilot readiness checklist and risk inventory
Model transition timeline and rollback criteria
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-11-03 15:00 UTC | Duration: 62 minutes | Recorders: Fireflies.ai
Attendees: Maya, Ravi, Leah - Redwood; Carlos, Priya, Daniel, Ava - BlueArc

00:00 Maya: hey everybody thanks for making time, we'll kick off, uh quick agenda, stability signals, then pilot risk inventory, then next steps.  I see we have the finance team on too.
00:18 Carlos: yep thanks, Carlos here, want to make sure we get to the cost bits early, we had a big surprise on our last month bill.
00:25 Leah: got it, we'll cover token-level breakouts and the embedding anomaly, Ravi you wanna start on the spike?
00:31 Ravi: sure, yeah so quick snapshot, last 90 days we saw a 3x spike in chat generation at 8pm UTC window, looks like prefix caching wasn't hitting as much as we expected, there's some session churn.
00:46 Priya: that matches our product rollout timing, we pushed a new conversation flow last month — maybe that's correlated.
00:53 Daniel: can you confirm which pool that traffic hit, dedicated or hosted? We thought it would stay on hosted.
01:00 Ravi: main bulk landed on the dedicated pool for BlueArc (your reserved GPUs), there was a routing policy flip when capacity hit 85% so some spilled to the lower-cost shard but with different model quant profile, that increased latency variance.
01:20 Carlos: ah the spillover — ok that explains the latency blips, but not the cost jump on embeddings.
01:27 Maya: quick note, embedding jobs were run as a nightly batch and one job accidentally ran in streaming mode, so cost per embedding soared — we have a ticket for that.
01:39 Ava: can you send the ticket id? finance needs line-items for the vendor reconciliation.
01:44 Leah: yes, action item: Leah to post embed-job ticket and attach raw cost file.
01:50 Carlos: perfect.
02:05 Ravi: back to latency — there was a P1 incident last week where tail latency hit 6s for 2-minute windows. Root cause was KV cache thrash on the dedicated pool when we had many short-lived sessions. The runtime's caching policy can be tuned, we proposed increasing sticky-session TTL and enabling prefix KV caching for the top three routes.
02:29 Daniel: ``K V cachee''? (laughter) sorry, kidding - how fast is that change to flip?
02:34 Ravi: we can push a config change to the bluearc cluster in a canary within 2 hours, full rollout in 24-36 hours assuming metrics look stable.
02:44 Priya: what are rollback criteria? We can't risk increasing cost if it backfires.
02:50 Maya: good point — rollback if p95 increases >10% or cost per 1k tokens increases by >15% in the canary window. We'll capture both metrics.
03:05 Carlos: on the embedding anomaly, we need a permanent guardrail so nightly jobs can't accidentally flip to streaming; is that something you can enforce?
03:13 Ravi: yes, we can add an upload-mode whitelist and gating on the S3 ingest path, plus a warning in the console.
03:23 Ava: finance also wants to track amortized GPU seconds per run; can you surface that?
03:29 Leah: we have a per-route cost dashboard coming in the console preview — will share link.
03:35 Maya: OK moving to pilot risk inventory — we split risks into operational, cost, security. I'll read off items and we can mark owners.
03:45 Maya: operational: routing spillover under high concurrency; caching TTL mismatch; model warmup time contributing to tail latency.
03:56 Carlos: add session affinity mismatch with our NLB, that's bitten us before.
04:02 Maya: noted. cost risks: embedding batch misconfiguration; quantization profile mismatch leading to worse quality and re-runs; burst autoscaling hitting burst caps and incurring overage fees.
04:16 Priya: quality regressions are a show-stopper, what's the plan to validate quality post-quant?
04:22 Ravi: SEs will run a canary eval suite of our production prompts + backstop: if ROUGE/semantic-sim drops >3% we'll auto-fallback to baseline model. We also keep token-level diffs.
04:36 Daniel: from infra side, we need a runbook for fallback — is that automated?
04:41 Maya: yes, automatic fallback policy exists in the rollout config; we can set thresholds per-route for immediate fallback.
04:49 Priya: timeline? We want pilot to start first week of Dec.
04:53 Maya: that's feasible if we complete the stress tests and finance sign-off this month.
05:02 Ava: sign-off depends on a deterministic cost estimate for the pilot — not a 95% CI, we want a line-item run-rate. Doable?
05:11 Leah: we'll generate a pilot cost model; need expected QPS, p95 tokens per request, and duration. Carlos can provide QPS.
05:19 Carlos: I'll share the traffic profile by EOD Thursday.
05:24 Maya: great. Security items?
05:28 Daniel: we need to validate KMS integration for private key usage and confirm that audit logs include per-token routing metadata for our SOC process.
05:39 Ravi: KMS integration is supported, and we already stream audit logs to your SIEM in test — we can add per-token routing if you want, though note that increases log volume.
05:51 Daniel: please provide volume estimates so security can sign off.
05:56 Maya: action: Ravi to produce audit log volume projection for per-token metadata.
06:02 Priya: also SSO test — we had intermittent SAML assertion failures last quarter, any update?
06:08 Leah: support ran a replay and traced it to our IdP certificate rotation window, we've patched and will run a smoke test with your SAML test account tomorrow.
06:18 Priya: thanks.
06:24 Maya: ok let's walk the prioritized risk list and owners quickly.
06:28 Maya: 1) Embedding batch misconfig (HIGH) — owner Leah, due 2026-11-10.
06:35 Leah: confirmed.
06:37 Maya: 2) KV cache thrash mitigations (HIGH) — owner Ravi, canary 2026-11-04.
06:45 Ravi: will do.
06:46 Maya: 3) Cost model for pilot (HIGH) — owner Leah + Ava, draft 2026-11-08.
06:54 Ava: noted.
06:56 Maya: 4) SAML smoke test and IdP cert window (MED) — owner Leah, done by 2026-11-04.
07:06 Leah: on it.
07:08 Maya: 5) Audit log volume projection for per-token routing (MED) — owner Ravi, 2026-11-06.
07:17 Ravi: yep.
07:19 Carlos: can we get an SLA for the pilot window? We need a written uptime target and crediting mechanism.
07:26 Maya: for pilot we can offer a 99.5% target with credits for degradation tied to incident postmortems; legal will draft a pilot addendum.
07:36 Carlos: sounds ok.
07:39 Priya: do we have a recommended rollback playbook in the case quality drops?
07:44 Ravi: yes, immediate rollback to baseline model, plus a staged backfill to replay requests for diffs; we automate the rollback if thresholds hit.
07:55 Priya: what about monitoring? We need per-route quality alerts and a dashboard.
07:59 Leah: we'll provision a private dashboard for BlueArc with those alert hooks.
08:06 Maya: last section — open questions and blockers.
08:09 Ava: finance wants to see previous three months of committed vs actual token usage to model burn.
08:16 Leah: action: Leah to export committed vs actual usage and annotate anomalies by 2026-11-05.
08:24 Carlos: we also need to finalize the burst policy for dedicated pool: can we set a soft limit?
08:31 Maya: yes, we can set soft burst with alerting and a hard cap to prevent runaway charges.
08:37 Daniel: include an automated throttle option tied to cost thresholds — if cost per minute exceeds X, throttle non-critical routes.
08:46 Ravi: we can implement route-level throttles; will include in the runbook.
08:51 Maya: ok, recap of next steps and owners...
09:00 Maya: Leah will share the embed ticket and cost file (due 2026-11-04); Leah & Ava to draft cost model (2026-11-08); Ravi to push KV cache canary (2026-11-04) and audit log projection (2026-11-06); Carlos to share traffic profile (2026-11-05).
09:21 Carlos: I'll get that out.
09:25 Priya: schedule for stress test? we want it before Dec 1.
09:30 Maya: propose stress test week Nov 22-26 — Leah to coordinate and we'll set a dry run Nov 19.
09:38 Leah: calendar invites after this.
09:41 Maya: any other items?
09:44 Daniel: one more — can we get a sample of the quantization recommendation report? need to see tradeoffs.
09:50 Ravi: yes, I'll attach a short tech note and a sample before Friday.
09:55 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up via the shared deck and action tracker. Meeting adjourned.
